implemented_requirements.evidence: connect_four.py defines ROWS = 6, COLS = 7 and initializes self.grid as a 6×7 list of zeros.
ConnectFour.current starts at 1 and switch() toggles between 1 and 2; main loop calls game.switch() after each non‑winning move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py get_move() prompts with input() and parses an integer column number.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range, numeric, not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: get_move() checks ValueError, ensures 0 ≤ col < COLS, and uses game.is_full(col) to reject full columns.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop disc into the chosen column, updating the board
implemented_requirements.evidence: ConnectFour.drop(col) finds the lowest empty row, writes the current player's id, and returns the row; render() prints the updated grid after each drop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect horizontal, vertical, and diagonal four‑in‑a‑row wins
implemented_requirements.evidence: ConnectFour.check_win(row, col) scans in four directions (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) counting consecutive discs; returns True when count ≥ 4.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: ConnectFour.full() returns True when the top row of every column is occupied; main loop ends with a draw message if full() is true.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game on win or draw
implemented_requirements.evidence: In main(), after each move the code checks check_win() and full(); on either condition it prints a message and breaks the loop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Provide a command‑line interface that updates after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: render(game) prints the board and column numbers after every drop; the loop continuously calls render().

judge.summary: The submitted code implements a complete, functional Connect Four game matching the benchmark description. All core features—grid size, turn alternation, input handling, move validation, board updates, win/draw detection, and termination—are present and demonstrably coded. The program is syntactically correct and appears ready to run, so the verdict is PASS.
